fields.label: Symbol
fields.description: The symbol used for this command.
fields.context: Case-sensitive action identity. The subcategory symbol receives a numbered runtime suffix in each visible command list. Use a nonempty unique action name such as journal for a new custom action and provide its handler. Native actions include item, skill, equip, status, formation, options, save and gameEnd. The special subcategory symbol creates category entries. Duplicate ordinary symbols share the scene handler and forced visibility/enabled overrides, so avoid them for independently controlled actions.

fields.label: Subcategory
fields.description: The subcategory used for this command. Leave empty for no subcategory.
fields.context: To define a category, create a complete command entry with Symbol subcategory, ExtJS returning its category name (for example return "tools";), and CallHandlerJS calling this.setSubcategory(arguments[0]);. Give child commands Subcategory "tools". Matching is case-sensitive. Without a matching category command, those children appear in the root menu. See MM-P-16 for complete-entry authoring.

fields.label: Icon
fields.description: Icon used for this command. Use 0 for no icon.
fields.context: Use the zero-based icon index in img/system/IconSet.png (16 columns, native 32-by-32 cells). A positive index draws that cell; 0 draws no icon. Choose an existing cell within the image; an out-of-sheet index does not provide a usable icon.

fields.label: STR: Text
fields.description: Displayed text used for this menu command. If this has a value, ignore the JS: Text version.
fields.context: Empty text and the native Untitled sentinel select TextJS; any other string is displayed directly.

fields.label: JS: Text
fields.description: JavaScript code used to determine string used for the displayed name.

fields.context: No arguments. Return the displayed text; used when TextStr is empty or Untitled. The function body runs in the game global context. Configure prerequisites before entering the menu; restart after editing plugin parameters.

fields.context: One argument: arguments[0] is the evaluated extension. Runs after actor confirmation. Read the selected actor with this._statusWindow.actor(this._statusWindow.index()); the native menuActor assignment occurs after this callback. The function body runs in the game global context. Configure prerequisites before entering the menu; restart after editing plugin parameters. This callback runs only after personal actor selection. Its command must start that selection, for example CallHandlerJS: this.callHandler(this.currentSymbol()); (with a native personal symbol such as skill). After the user chooses an actor, PersonalHandlerJS runs with the Scene_Menu receiver and the selected actor available through this._statusWindow.actor(this._statusWindow.index()).

No fields are implicitly filled in a new entry.

examples: main-menu parameters set --project <game> --path /Variable/WindowRect --value '"return new Rectangle(0, this.mainAreaBottom() - this.calcWindowHeight(1, false), this.mainCommandWidth(), this.calcWindowHeight(1, false));"'

parameters.context: The default on this containing parameter is the native complete preset used when it is absent or reset as a whole. Each nested field retains its separate native editor default, used when that field is absent or reset individually; these defaults can differ. Read parameters get for the currently effective value. A set replaces the selected value and requires every field in a struct, including unchanged editorial labels. The historical nativeDefault preset contains AdjustCommandHeight:func. The supported boolean field uses storageKey AdjustCommandHeight:eval; CLI authoring writes that canonical key. Native preset text is retained as reference metadata, not input to --value.

parameters.label: Command Window Style
parameters.description: Choose the positioning and style of the Main Menu Command Window. This will automatically rearrange windows.

parameters.label: Command Style Settings
parameters.description: Settings for the non-default Command Window Styles.

fields.label: Command Style
fields.description: How do you wish to draw command entries in the Command Window?
fields.context: Style auto checks each formatted command name: without an icon escape it draws text; with an icon it draws icon plus text when the measured name fits the item line width, otherwise only the icon. /CommandWindowStyle chooses the overall layout; /CustomCmdWin/Style chooses content drawing inside each command.

fields.label: Text Alignment
fields.description: Decide how you want the text to be aligned.

fields.label: Rows
fields.description: Number of visible rows.
fields.context: Rows affects top and bottom layouts. thinTop and thinBottom always use one row; default uses the native command rectangle. The mobile layout also uses Rows when calculating its centered command-window height.

fields.label: Columns
fields.description: Number of maximum columns.
fields.context: Cols affects top, bottom and mobile layouts. thinTop and thinBottom instead use one column per current command, and default uses the native single column.

fields.label: Mobile Thickness
fields.description: The thickness of the buttons for mobile version.
fields.context: This is a line-height multiplier, not pixels: mobile command item height is lineHeight() * MobileThickness + 8 pixels (5 with the native 36-pixel line height gives 188 pixels). Applies when /CommandWindowStyle is mobile, on desktop too; it does not detect the device platform.

parameters.context: Style auto checks each formatted command name: without an icon escape it draws text; with an icon it draws icon plus text when the measured name fits the item line width, otherwise only the icon. /CommandWindowStyle chooses the overall layout; /CustomCmdWin/Style chooses content drawing inside each command. MobileThickness affects only the mobile layout; see MM-P-48.

commands.label: Actor: Change Menu Image (Group)
commands.description: Change the selected actors’ menu portrait filename in img/pictures, without its extension.

args.label: Actor ID(s)
args.description: Select which Actor ID(s) to affect.

args.label: Filename
args.description: Selected actor(s) will have their menu images changed to this.
args.context: Picture filename without extension in img/pictures; for example Actor1_1 requires img/pictures/Actor1_1.png. Empty string clears the explicit portrait rather than restoring the actor note image; native graphics or compatible class/equipment portrait providers may then apply.

commands.context: Runs at the native interpreter command. Group and range ignore missing/nonpositive IDs. Range includes both endpoints regardless of order. Legacy JS evaluates expressions and flattens one array level. Current JS evaluates ActorJS first; FilenameJS runs only for an existing actor. CLI stores JavaScript without executing it. The example requires actors 1 and 2 (only actor 1 for the current JS command), an existing common event 1, and img/pictures/Actor1_1.png. An empty filename clears the explicit portrait; native graphic fallback and compatible class/equipment portrait providers may then apply. It does not restore the original actor note image.
examples: main-menu commands insert --project <game> --target common-event:1 --before 0 --command ChangeActorMenuImageGroup --value '{"Step1":[1,2],"Step2":"Actor1_1"}' --expected-hash HASH_FROM_LIST

tags.label: Menu image or portrait
tags.description: Actor Note portrait settings; Image and Portrait spellings are equivalent. Individual axis offsets override the paired offset. Use explicit signs and native spaces.
tags.context: Read from the actor database Note. Filename is stored on actor initialization and can be replaced by image commands; offsets remain note-based. Put the resource in img/pictures; omit its extension in the tag. The example requires img/pictures/Actor1_1.png.
tags.syntax: Pass the complete tag as a JSON string.
tags.occurrences: First matching tag for each variant wins; individual axes take precedence over paired offsets.
tags.selection: Use --occurrence for duplicate physical entries; unrelated note bytes are preserved.

tags.label: Paired portrait offset
tags.description: Actor Note portrait settings; Image and Portrait spellings are equivalent. Individual axis offsets override the paired offset. Use explicit signs and native spaces.
tags.context: Read from the actor database Note. Filename is stored on actor initialization and can be replaced by image commands; offsets remain note-based. Offsets are measured in source picture pixels, with X first and Y second in the paired tag. Positive X moves the image right and negative X left; positive Y moves it down and negative Y up within the portrait crop. Individual axis tags override that axis of the paired tag.
tags.syntax: Pass the complete tag as a JSON string.
tags.occurrences: First matching tag for each variant wins; individual axes take precedence over paired offsets.
tags.selection: Use --occurrence for duplicate physical entries; unrelated note bytes are preserved.
